newsitem.title: INDIA: Suicide threat stays as court clears Miss World.
newsitem.headline: Suicide threat stays as court clears Miss World.

text.p: An Indian woman reiterated a threat to burn herself to death in protest against Miss World coming to India after a court on Tuesday said the beauty pageant could go-ahead in the southern city of Bangalore.

"My protests will be peaceful. By burning myself I will not be disrupting the show. We will go-ahead with our earlier plan," Kina Narayana Shashikala, leader of the Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women) told Reuters after a court rejected the activist group's petition to block the show.
The traditionalist group had held its threat of self immolation in abeyance until the court decision was known.
"We declined to ban the show," chief justice of the Karnataka high court R.P. Sethi told a packed courtroom. "The state government should not prevent peaceful protests."

Shashikala has threatened that a number of her followers will infiltrate the 20,000 crowd expected to attend the Miss World crowning ceremony on November 23 and take cyanide pills before setting themselves ablaze.
The protesters argue that the beauty contest demeans women and is offensive to Indian culture.
